Regal Cineworld Group faced a critical challenge after emerging, like many other businesses, from the sizable impact COVID-19 left on the industry. 

The technological leaps noted with the likes of mass adoption of chatbots, AI, Zoom and customers moving to more digital methods of communication, expedited the need for sudden change in how the business interacted with customers. 

It was identified that the company had outdated customer communication tools and in some territories, none. Insufficient tools were use,d which provide slow response times and create inefficiencies in managing thousands of daily queries across the globe. This impacted customer satisfaction and limited our ability to deliver a seamless experience, something we take pride in delivering. 

To overcome this, we implemented Freshworks, creating a unified platform that replaced fragmented systems. In some instances, there were no systems. Excel sheets, documents stored locally that were inaccurate or out of date and even Microsoft Outlook to respond to customers! These were the means of managing customer interactions and caused continual confusion, mistakes and risks to the business. There were also no insights or clear data as to trend analysis or even contact quantity. 

Freshworks enabled real-time communication, automated workflows, and advanced analytics, allowing us to streamline operations and gain actionable insights into customer behavior.

By leveraging Freshworks, we integrated automation and AI-driven insights into our service model, ensuring faster, smarter, and more personalized interactions. Our approach demonstrates how innovation can scale customer experience without compromising quality, providing instant answers to customer queries, some extremely basic, but often leaving customers to wait hours or days for a response, instead of seconds.

column17:
At One&Only Royal Mirage, email is one of the most influential touchpoints in the guest journey. High-value bookings, travel partner requests, and pre-arrival needs all flow through the reservations inbox. Yet the system we had in place was manual, unstructured, and impossible to measure. Backlogs formed quickly, quality varied between agents, and leaders lacked visibility into what guests were actually asking for. For a Forbes-rated luxury resort, this wasn’t just an operational gap—it was a risk to the brand experience.

The goal wasn’t to simply “respond faster.” It was to rebuild the entire communication engine behind reservations.

Freshdesk became the platform that made this possible. Instead of a single broad 24-hour response target, we introduced a structured SLA model based on the type of guest, the nature of the request, sender category, and automated keyword detection. Workflows now prioritize urgent booking decisions, escalate time-sensitive communications, and instantly route rate checks, amendments, cancellations, and payment queries to the right specialists.

This shift created measurable impact. Backlog reduced by 35% because agents no longer wasted time sorting or guessing priorities. Accuracy improved dramatically, supported by automated categorization, cleaner handovers, and consistent templates. Quality audit scores increased by an estimated 20% due to brand-aligned responses and real-time coaching opportunities. The team gained more than two hours of productive time per agent each week because Freshdesk eliminated manual triage. And conversion-related inquiries received priority handling, leading to faster confirmations during peak demand periods and a noticeable uplift in revenue-capturing decisions.

What makes this project award-worthy is the scale of transformation. Freshdesk wasn’t deployed as a ticketing tool but as the operational backbone of the reservations function. It brought structure, intelligence, and predictability to a channel that previously depended on individual habits and manual effort. It elevated both team performance and the guest experience, making every interaction more timely, accurate, and aligned with luxury service expectations.

Freshdesk helped us turn a high-touch, high-stakes communication channel into a disciplined, scalable, insight-driven system positioning One&Only Royal Mirage to deliver exceptional service with consistency and confidence.

The "New Starter Automation Rollout" for Lovisa implemented a new, system-triggered onboarding process for IT, HR, and Payroll, specifically focusing on account creation for retail store staff.


Challenge Overcome:


The primary challenge was to automate the onboarding process and eliminate human error and the negative downstream effects caused by inconsistent or incorrect data entry (e.g., spelling mistakes, inconsistent use of case) in the forms outside of the Freshworks platform. These errors would lead to the creation of incorrect user accounts in multiple systems. 


Innovative or Unique Aspect:


The project features a highly innovative and unique design choice: a deliberate manual intervention (an agent-triggered task status change) was incorporated into the automation flow. This step forces the IT agent to manually review the new starter data for quality and correctness before the automated account creation process is triggered in Freshservice. This counter-intuitive step within a full automation is a clever strategy to safeguard the process against poor data quality originating from external systems, ensuring clean and correct account setup.


How Freshworks Was Able to Help:


The project was entirely built on the Freshworks Freshservice platform. Freshservice facilitated:
Workflow Automation: Creating the end-to-end automation, including system-triggered ticket creation from the external application..
Communication: Designing and sending out highly formatted, role-specific welcome emails directly from Freshservice.
Control: The core workflow logic, which incorporates the mandatory agent review checkpoint, is managed within the Freshservice process configuration.
Overview of the Benefits:
Elimination of Human Error: Achieved the primary goal of preventing errors in account creation and the subsequent negative impact on other applications.
Improved User Experience (Intangible Benefit): The automation, including the timely delivery of correct welcome emails and accounts, is expected to improve the new starter experience, which is a key factor in employee confidence and can positively impact turnover, especially in the high-turnover retail space.
Rollout Success: The system-triggered accounts have been successfully created, with the new process now live for a large volume of new hires.

My advocacy has always extended far beyond external visibility. At Refresh 2024, our IT & Library teams and our Finance Helpdesk were fully onboarded onto Freshservice. Building on that momentum, I went on to lead the onboarding of both our Student Experience Helpdesk and our HR department. These transitions have been major organisational achievements, but their success was rooted in sustained, passionate advocacy—both for Freshservice as a product and for the transformative benefits it brings to staff and more importantly, our students. I take pride in ensuring our agents view Freshservice not simply as a ticketing tool, but as a strategic enabler of excellent customer service and a framework that strengthens collaboration across the university.

A key challenge in nurturing widespread adoption is bridging the knowledge gap between Freshworks’ continuous product enhancements and the agents using the platform daily. Monthly release notes are invaluable for administrators, but agents often lack clarity on what is available, what requires configuration, or what will realistically be implemented locally. To address this, I introduced quarterly feature update sessions specifically tailored to our agent community. These sessions go beyond highlighting new capabilities, they spotlight upcoming roadmap items, internal improvement initiatives, and areas where agent feedback can shape future development. By embedding a dedicated feedback loop within the sessions, we’ve empowered agents to raise concerns, report pain points, and influence our configuration direction. Items we cannot resolve internally are escalated to our CSM, ensuring their voices feed directly into Freshworks. The positive response to these sessions has been overwhelming, and I regularly encourage other Freshservice administrators (through the Insider Program and even during discussions on monthly release notes) to adopt similar practices.

Thought leadership also means evolving in step with the platform’s capabilities. When Freshservice introduced the Major Incident ticket type, I immediately recognised an opportunity to modernise and elevate our existing process. I led a full redesign that not only leveraged the new Major Incident framework, but also integrated on call schedules to ensure Incident Managers received real time phone alerts for emerging issues. At the same time, I implemented the automated alert management system, enabling previously separate features to function as a cohesive response mechanism. Together, these enhancements transformed our Major Incident workflow, significantly improving response times and creating a more streamlined, reliable resolution pathway.

This is just one example of how I continuously harness new Freshservice functionality to deliver measurable, user centred improvements. During beta testing of Agentic AI on Freshservice Support Portals, I identified its potential to provide 24/7 guided support by connecting students with relevant knowledge articles and service requests. However, we also recognised a challenge: our support portal historically received limited traffic, largely because our helpdesks respond exceptionally well to email based enquiries.

To maximise the value of Agentic AI, I designed a solution to embed this functionality directly into our award winning student mobile application. In doing so we placed the entire Freshservice knowledge base, along with AI driven support, literally in the pocket of every student on campus. Coupled with the expanded onboarding of departmental helpdesks, this ensures students have immediate access to accurate information, relevant services, and streamlined support, right alongside daily essentials like student cards and class timetables. It represents a step change in how our university connects students with the help they need.

1. The Challenge

In late 2025, our support environment faced a convergence of risks common to high-growth fintechs but rarely addressed holistically:

High-volume customer demand (17,000–19,000 tickets per month)

Concentration in financially sensitive issues (withdrawals, FICA, access to funds)

Heavy reliance on automation and chatbot deflection

Seasonal staffing constraints

Rising negative sentiment in public app reviews

While our operational metrics remained stable, external sentiment revealed a deeper issue:
customers were not angry about bugs or complexity — they were angry about silence when money was involved.

This created a dual risk:

Reputational risk (“scam” language, public escalation)

Regulatory risk (ombudsman threats linked to unresolved withdrawal issues)

2. Our Approach

Rather than treating support, automation, sentiment, and calls as separate channels, we deliberately connected all signals into one operating model.

What we changed:

1. Data-led visibility
We analysed:

Ticket volumes and backlog trends

SLA performance

Bot deflection and escalation rates

Bot CSAT vs agent CSAT

App store sentiment

Call handling data after publishing a contact number

This allowed us to identify where automation helped — and where it actively increased frustration.

2. Strategic human access
We made a deliberate decision to publish a direct contact number in Freshdesk responses during December — not as a full call centre rollout, but as a targeted trust intervention.

3. Priority-based escalation
We shifted focus from “fastest response” to financial-risk triage, prioritising:

Withdrawals

Bank verification

Account access

3. What Was Innovative

Treating negative sentiment as an operational input, not a reputational afterthought

Using short human conversations as a de-escalation tool rather than a resolution channel

Proving that visible human access reduces rage faster than automation alone

Measuring the real impact of publishing a phone number instead of assuming cost or chaos

This balanced automation efficiency with trust-critical human moments — a key challenge in regulated fintech environments.

4. Results & Impact
Operational Stability

Tickets resolved consistently exceeded tickets created (Dec & Jan)

Backlog remained low and controlled

SLA within 3 business days held between 86%–91%, even during volume spikes

January post-holiday demand rebounded sharply — and was absorbed without collapse

Chatbot Performance

Chatbot deflected a significant portion of demand

Bot CSAT: 73% (1,299 responses)

Demonstrated strong performance for simple and Tier-1 queries

Human Support Validation

After publishing the contact number:

3,098 inbound calls answered

Average talk time: ~1 min 51 sec

Calls were short, resolution-focused, and de-escalating

This disproved the assumption that phone access leads to long, unmanageable calls.

Customer Experience Insight

Agent CSAT: 61.3%

Negative sentiment concentrated around escalations, not initial contact

App reviews confirmed the core issue was support visibility during financial stress, not product quality alone

5. Key Learning

Customers will tolerate bugs, complexity, and learning curves.
They will not tolerate silence when their money is involved.

Automation is effective — but trust in financial services requires visible human access at the right moment.

6. Why This Matters

This initiative demonstrates how fintech support teams can:

Maintain efficiency at scale

Use automation responsibly

Reduce reputational and regulatory risk

Improve customer trust without abandoning digital channels

It provides a replicable model for blending automation and human support in high-risk, high-volume environments.

7. Conclusion

By combining operational metrics, sentiment analysis, chatbot data, and call handling evidence, we moved from reactive support to intentional trust management.

The result was a more resilient support operation — and a clearer understanding that customer experience is not just speed, but visibility and reassurance when it matters most.

Our team transformed a fragmented, accountability-driven challenge into a seamless, omni-channel service ecosystem that connects sales, support, and customers on a single platform.

The Challenge

We were using Freshsales Suite primarily for sales communication, with customer emails handled by the sales team. However, there was no structured accountability or SLA governance, leading to delayed responses, customer frustration, and lost revenue opportunities. Support requests arrived through multiple channels—email, calls, and chats—but without a unified system, tickets were missed, duplicated, or handled by multiple agents simultaneously, creating confusion for both customers and internal teams.

The Vision

Our vision was to build a single, unified ecosystem that delivers a true omni-channel experience—where customers can reach us through any channel and receive timely, consistent support. We aimed to automate workflows, reduce response SLAs, introduce measurable and realistic KPIs for every team member, and seamlessly transition from manual processes to an intelligent, automated service model.

How Freshworks Helped

By implementing Freshdesk Enterprise alongside Freshsales Suite, Freshchat, and Freshcaller, we unified all customer interactions into one platform. Freshdesk became the central hub for customer queries, enabling intelligent ticket routing, automation, and SLA enforcement. Freshsales provided complete visibility into customer conversations and sales discussions, allowing our sales team to engage with customers more authentically and contextually.

This integration eliminated manual handoffs, ensured zero unanswered tickets, and enabled our teams to resolve and close more tickets than ever before. The result has been a significant improvement in customer satisfaction, reflected in strong feedback on Google and Shoppers Approved.

Innovation & Uniqueness

What makes this project unique is how we eliminated chaos at scale. Previously, group inboxes led to duplicate efforts and inconsistent customer communication. We redesigned the workflow by linking support emails to structured groups, implementing round-robin and skill-based routing, and applying differentiated SLA policies based on lead value and urgency.

Canned responses improved response speed and consistency, while also creating reusable documentation to onboard new agents faster. Most importantly, we achieved unprecedented scalability—handling higher volumes of support and sales interactions without increasing headcount.

Business & Experience Impact

The impact has been transformational. Despite operating in one of the most challenging business years, we achieved 40% year-over-year revenue growth, proving that exceptional service directly fuels business success. Customers now trust that they will receive a response within two hours, significantly improving confidence and loyalty.

Our sales team unlocked new revenue channels, our operations team eliminated duplication through Magento 2 API integrations, and leadership gained deeper insights by connecting Freshsales data to Power BI for advanced reporting and decision-making.

This project exemplifies the Dream Team Award by showing how a high-performing team can uncomplicate work, connect employees and customers, and deliver seamless service experiences through the combined power of Freshservice/Freshdesk-led service excellence and Freshsales-driven customer engagement.

Jonathan Rodriguez, Director of Global Innovation & Product Development at DHL, stands out as a powerful nominee for the Experience Transformation Leader award by demonstrating a clear vision, driving measurable results, and implementing a truly innovative human-AI partnership. His leadership is not merely about adopting new technology, but strategically guiding DHL's massive global scale-up toward a standardized, AI-enabled service model.

The Transformation Challenge: Redefining Service Quality


Before his intervention, DHL faced significant customer service hurdles:
Agent Bandwidth: Heavy reliance on email for support, which saw low-value, repetitive L0 and L1 queries consume precious agent time.
Operational Inefficiency: Regional process variations and slow change management resulted in key performance indicators (KPIs) trailing industry benchmarks.
System Fragmentation: The company was grappling with complex issues, including a dual-system dependency and a massive technical debt of over 1,500 automation rules.
Mr. Rodriguez recognized this challenge as a strategic opportunity to redefine both the customer and employee experience. His core objective was to drive digitalization, standardization, and maximize ROI to support DHL’s goal of doubling operations in five years.

The Innovative Solution: A Human-AI Partnership


Mr. Rodriguez’s vision was clear: to leverage AI not to replace agents, but to elevate them. The resulting innovation was the implementation of Freshworks solutions with a people-first AI strategy:
Elevating the Agent: Freddy AI Copilot was deployed to streamline support operations through auto-triage, reducing manual assignment friction. Agents now leverage Copilot's features to summarize, rephrase, and enhance tone, enabling them to focus on complex, high-value interactions.
Volume Deflection: The pilot Chatbot deployment achieved a 70% automated resolution rate (well above the 60% industry benchmark), with an 85% effective resolution rate including drop-offs—a clear proof point for automation ROI.
Standardization & Governance: His team is actively leading the transition to a global Command Center structure and driving high-priority actions like the redesign of SLA policies (especially pause rules) and a commitment to reduce automation rules by 50%.
The Measurable Impact: Transformative Results


The strategic human-AI partnership and standardization efforts have yielded results that are not just qualitative; they are highly measurable and transformative:

Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) is a strong 96.39% (Industry Trendsetter levels!).
First Assign Time was drastically reduced from 1.5 hours to a mere 19 minutes.
First Response Time dropped from 5 hours to 1 hour and 31 minutes.

Under his leadership, DHL’s human-AI partnership has delivered speed and satisfaction, successfully enhancing service quality and scaling operations efficiently. His team's forward-looking approach, with the imminent launch of Agentic Workflows and Email AI Agent, solidifies his position as a leader who has redefined experience and set a new standard for global logistics.

Conclusion: A True Transformation Leader


Mr. Rodriguez has successfully championed the crucial belief that “By leveraging AI to handle repetitive tasks, DHL empowers agents to focus on complex, high-value interactions, enhancing human customer service rather than replacing it.”


His team's forward-looking approach—including a strategic plan to revisit the Email AI Agent co-design, scale the chatbot architecture globally, and align the entire organization to a data-driven Command Center model—solidifies his position as a leader who has redefined experience and set a new, scalable standard for global logistics. He is successfully balancing aggressive business growth with a thoughtful, measured approach to technology adoption, ensuring transformation delivers immediate, measurable ROI.

Zaggle a Startup from India was founded in 2011 with a clear and enduring vision: to simplify and bring discipline, transparency, and control to the way organizations manage business spends. From the outset, Zaggle focused on building strong foundations in the prepaid and loyalty ecosystem, combining regulatory compliance with practical, enterprise-ready use cases. This early innovation was globally recognized in 2013 when Zaggle won the Global Prepaid Exchange Award for Start-up of the Year. In 2015, the launch of the Zaggle app marked a significant milestone in digitizing loyalty and cashback-led spend experiences. In 2017, Zaggle further strengthened its brand presence and market credibility by signing national sports icons Jasprit Bumrah, Hardik Pandya, and Mohammed Siraj as brand ambassadors, reinforcing trust and visibility among enterprises and users alike. By 2018, Zaggle had firmly entered the enterprise space with the launch of its corporate website and structured platforms for employee benefits and expense management.
In 2019, Zaggle accelerated its evolution as an enterprise fintech platform with the introduction of PROPEL, its rewards, recognition, and engagement solution, along with an expense management card powered by IndusInd Bank. This innovation was recognized as the Best B2B Enterprise Product of 2019, reinforcing Zaggle’s growing relevance among large organizations. The momentum continued into 2020, when Zaggle won the Best FinTech Corporate Innovation Program Award at The Economic Times BFSI Innovation Tribe Awards, further establishing its credibility as a trusted and scalable enterprise fintech partner.
As Zaggle scaled, it made a conscious shift from being a product-led fintech to becoming a platform-driven enterprise spend management company. A key enabler of this transformation was its deliberate and multi-layered acquisition strategy, designed to strengthen capabilities across the entire spend and payments value chain. Zaggle strategically integrated six complementary acquisitions and investments into its ecosystem: TaxSpanner, strengthening tax compliance and filings; 86400 (Mobileware), enhancing digital payments and financial infrastructure; Dice, adding advanced technology capabilities; Rio, expanding digital and engagement-led solutions; EffiaSoft, contributing specialized enterprise software depth; and GreenEdge Enterprises, reinforcing emerging and sustainability-aligned business segments. Each acquisition was purpose-driven, accelerating innovation while maintaining a unified and scalable platform architecture.
The period between 2022 and 2023 marked a defining phase in Zaggle’s journey. In 2022, Zaggle launched Zoyer, simplifying and automating B2B payments for enterprises and SMEs. In 2023, Zaggle achieved a major milestone with a successful IPO and listing on both the NSE and BSE, recording its highest-ever annual revenue and PAT, while remaining profitable for five consecutive years. The same year also saw the launch of the YES Bank–Zaggle Corporate Credit Card and Zaggle ZatiX, its intelligent spend analytics platform—demonstrating Zaggle’s ability to scale innovation alongside public-market discipline.
Post-IPO, 2024 and 2025 reflect sustained momentum and strategic maturity. In 2024, Zaggle was selected as a winner of the Pride of Telangana Awards in the Startup category and recognized as ‘FinTech Brand of the Year’ at the BW Businessworld Festival of Fintech Conclave & Awards. During the same year, Zaggle acquired a 98% stake in TaxSpanner and made a strategic investment in 86400 (erstwhile Mobileware), while delivering more than 3X returns to investors since listing. In 2025, Zaggle continued its growth trajectory with additional investments in Mobileware Technologies, partnership launches with Thomas Cook India and SOTC Travel, continued acquisitions, and enhanced employee benefit offerings for users—demonstrating long-term commitment to ecosystem expansion and customer value.
Today, Zaggle stands as India’s #1 integrated Spend Management platform, uniquely combining SaaS and fintech at scale. The platform manages over ₹40,000 crore of business spends, serves more than 3,600 corporate customers and 3.5 million+ users, and has issued over 50 million cards through partnerships with 19 banking institutions. As India’s leading issuer of prepaid cards and a top issuer of corporate credit cards, Zaggle delivers measurable cost savings, enhanced compliance, and real-time visibility to organizations across industries and geographies.
At its core, Zaggle offers a comprehensive and continuously evolving suite of spend management solutions, spanning employee expenses, travel and expense management, Procure to Pay, Forex Services, Device Leasing Programme for Employee Benefits, Cashless OPD with Ekincare, rewards and recognition, channel partner incentives, fleet management, vendor payables, petty cash digitization, branch-level recurring expenses through BROME, utility payments, and international payments via Zaggle International Payments (ZIP). These solutions are unified through a single dashboard supported by mobile applications, APIs, and deep ERP and HRMS integrations.
Automation and intelligence power the platform through features such as smart OCR-based receipt capture, automated approvals, MCC and MID-level controls, real-time reconciliations, and audit trails. Through Zaggle ZatiX, enterprises gain transaction-level visibility, actionable spend insights, improved cash-flow control, and audit readiness.
Guided by a seasoned leadership team and strong institutional governance, Zaggle today represents the evolution of enterprise spend management in India—from fragmented tools to a unified, intelligent, and compliant digital ecosystem. As the journey continues, Zaggle remains firmly focused on its long-term ambition: to redefine how businesses plan, manage, and optimize every rupee they spend.

Customer Story: The Sanger Institute’s Freshservice Transformation

Overview
In June 2024, the Wellcome Sanger Institute successfully went live with Freshservice, marking a major step forward in modernising its service management landscape. Prior to implementation, the Institute relied on a fragmented mix of tools, including Cherwell and multiple email-based ticketing systems, which created inefficiencies, limited visibility, and inconsistent user experiences.
Freshservice was introduced to unify service delivery, improve governance, and enable automation across IT and business services.

IDS Phase 1: IT Onboarding and Core Service Management
The initial rollout focused on onboarding the IT department and establishing strong foundations through service creation, Change Advisory Board (CAB) processes, asset management and contract management.
The Institute implemented a robust two-stage CAB model:
Technical CAB, responsible for assessing the technical feasibility and risk of changes
Governance CAB, responsible for stakeholder engagement and communications approval
This approach has proven highly effective. Where delays occurred, they were typically due to manual handoffs after changes were completed. To resolve this, the team automated reminder workflows that notify agents when a change remains in a “pending release” state for 10 days—significantly improving closure rates and governance compliance.
CAB requests older than 10 days.   39% decrease in CAB requested not being moved from “Pending Release”. 

 The Metrics used for the above analytics, the only difference between graphs is the created date is changed to before/after


Operational AI Service Governance
With the rapid growth of AI solutions, the Institute was tasked with introducing stronger controls for AI software requests. Using Freshservice’s parallel approval functionality, the team designed a three-stage approval workflow for new AI tools.
Each approval stage includes structured questions, and the questions and responses are automatically passed to subsequent approvers. This ensures full transparency and allows every approver to make informed decisions based on shared information and prior assessments—strengthening governance without adding unnecessary friction.
As the 3-stage workflow has only recently been introduced, we don’t yet have sufficient data to directly compare current approval wait times with the previous manual/email-based process.
From a shadow AI perspective, the new workflow is already showing positive signs. We’ve worked closely with both the Cyber Security and Operational AI teams to improve visibility, governance, and compliance, which has helped reduce the number of unauthorised or unapproved AI tools being used across campus and lower overall business risk.

The 3-stage workflow has already been used several times to request new AI tools in an official and compliant manner. In addition, we now offer catalogue items for enterprise-licensed ChatGPT and Notebook LLM access, ensuring users are not relying on personal accounts. Together, these changes have made our AI tooling process more seamless, efficient, and transparent.


Improving Audio-Visual Service Requests
IT supports smaller audio-visual (AV) requests, while larger AV and all conference centre requests are handled by an external provider. Previously, customers submitted requests via a shared mailbox, which often led to confusion and incomplete information.
Working collaboratively with the director office, Comms team and our AV external provider, we designed a structured request form in Freshservice that captures all required details upfront. Submissions trigger an approval step within IT:
Approved requests are assigned to IT
Declined requests are automatically closed with a clear customer notification, however when declined the external provider receives the request details directly
AV support for our conference centre also outputs an informative email to the conference centre administrator so they are fully aware of the request that has been sent to Venue AV
This streamlined approach has improved clarity for users, reduced manual coordination with an external AV company saving on average 15 minutes per request as no meeting is now required.  The Service Desk agents had set questions to ask the customer but as these are now all within the new form this saves our agents on average 10 minutes to ticket.   We don’t get a high volume of requests for this service, around 45 per year but this does save us 18.75 hours in agent labour per year, The customer also saves time as the form now captures all requirements which means they don’t have to reply to set questions.     



Transition Away from Email-Based Ticketing
Several faculties, including Procurement, CASM and PAM, were previously operating entirely through email-based ticketing. These services were successfully migrated into Freshservice, bringing consistency, visibility, and reporting that were not previously possible.

Laboratory Asset Management: A Major Step Forward
One of the most impactful outcomes of the Freshservice implementation has been the introduction of formal laboratory asset management, an area that had not previously been centrally tracked.
Key requirements included:
Full asset visibility for IT assisting with compliance
Secure asset updates from a segregated network.  Older robots are still running Windows 7 due to the software not being compatible with Windows 10 and 11.  This keeps these vulnerable PCs safe and secure as they cannot speak to the outside world apart from allowing the asset to check in
Controlled access for lab managers, limited strictly to their own lab assets
To meet these needs, the Institute created a dedicated Freshservice workspace where each lab is represented as a group, with assets assigned accordingly. Lab managers are designated as asset owners, while IT retains full oversight.
To enable connectivity from segregated lab networks, the team partnered with networking colleagues to implement the necessary firewall changes.
This solution has delivered significant benefits for both IT security and lab operations, providing accurate asset tracking for the first time.   
Within a year this project will be complete, and this will enable us to be security compliant
Planned automation enhancements
Future improvements are already designed, including automated decommissioning workflows. When an asset is marked as decommissioned:
The lab manager receives a decommissioning service link
A collection ticket is automatically created for Service Delivery
Previously, this process relied on multiple manual steps involving emails, printed forms, scanning, and filing. Once released, the automated workflow is expected to save substantial time and effort.



SciOps faculty
This became part of the asset management project as SciOps have lots of robots in their labs.
The form was complicated due to the multiple vendors which had separate instruments which were dependent on the vendor and then each instrument would have different types of heads.  This was achieved via custom objects 
 And now when asset are added under SciOps they automatically appear in the custom object and the form


Automating Role Changes in UBW (ERP)
In the past month, MOBS received a total of 203 service tickets, 60 of which were related to role changes. These role-related requests accounted for approximately 30% of the team’s overall workload.
On average, each role change request previously required around 10 minutes of manual effort to process. By fully automating these 60 requests, the team is now saving approximately 10 hours of support time per month.
This measurable time saving allows the team to focus on higher-value work, particularly as they prepare for increased operational demands during major transformation initiatives.
MOBS were keen to implement an automated solution for UBW role changes ahead of 2026, a year expected to be exceptionally busy due to the organisation’s new ERP implementation project. With the new ERP project effectively becoming a full-time commitment, the team recognised that continuing to manually process UBW role changes would no longer be sustainable. Delays in handling these requests could directly impact users’ ability to raise requisitions or gain timely approval for financial transactions.
By automating the UBW role change process, MOBS have significantly reduced the administrative burden on support agents while also improving the experience for requesters. The new UBW role change forms in Freshservice are intelligently designed to display only active UBW users and active UBW project codes. This prevents invalid data from being submitted and eliminates requests for users or project codes that do not exist in the system.
As a result, the automation has not only saved time for the service team but has also streamlined the request journey for end users, ensuring faster, more reliable processing during a critical period of organisational change.






Travel Office Workspace
The Travel Office also transitioned from an email-based request model to a dedicated FreshService workspace, improving request tracking, accountability, and the overall user experience. By having the form on FreshService, we can mandate specific fields that the Travel Office needs in order to process their requests. As before, they would have to regularly go back to the customer asking them for more information that they need to process their request..
One of the main requirements for the Travel Office was the ability to print out their requests so that they could continue to work in a way that suited their needs. Initially we planned for them to simply print the ticket out using the print button, but this resulted in a format that wasn’t very easy to read or understand. We then looked into the new document template generation functionality within FreshService and found that we could upload the current Travel Office template and have it populated with the answers from the Travel Office request. 
This has enabled us to cater to our customers’ needs and let them work in the way they’re most comfortable, without disrupting their existing processes, while still gaining the tracking and accountability provided by Freshservice.
Another  ask for this request was to allow up to 5 approvers who were not the users managers as team administrators authorise these requests.  An informative email is sent to the users manager so they still get full visibility.



Analytics
Freshservice Analytics has proven extremely valuable across multiple areas of the business. Below are just a few of the ways it has helped us:
Asset Management
Security-focused software tracking, such as understanding how many devices are running a specific operating system
Visibility into device check-ins, helping us identify assets that are no longer reporting
Software asset tracking, including confirming whether users have been upgraded to newer versions of Microsoft Office
Customer Engagement
We now run our customer engagement meetings entirely using Freshservice Analytics
This allows us to present the data stakeholders actually want to see and provide clear reports on their usage of specific services
As a result, our meetings are more focused, more impactful, and enable us to proactively address issues before they arise
External Customer Charging
By leveraging workflows and business rules, we can now accurately report on external companies that are billed for our services
This has significantly streamlined a process that previously took 2–3 hours and now takes as little as 30 minutes, even on a busy day
Team Tracking
We distribute a weekly analytics report to internal teams covering SLA performance, current workload, and week-on-week trends
This visibility has given teams clearer targets and accountability, driving improvements that previously received less focus
FreshService Ticket to Monday.com item
SciOps Automation approached us with a request to streamline their workflow by transferring Freshservice tickets directly to their project board in monday.com. While Freshservice offers a built-in monday.com connector, we quickly discovered a key limitation: it only supported a single target board. This meant that if additional teams wanted the same functionality, all tickets would be forced into the same board—clearly not a scalable solution.

To overcome this, we explored the monday.com API and identified a more flexible approach. Using a web request node within a Freshservice workflow, we enabled the creation of monday.com board items dynamically. We also introduced a custom ticket dropdown field, “Create in monday.com?”, and configured the workflow to trigger when this value changes from any to Yes.

Once triggered, the workflow checks whether a monday.com item already exists for the ticket. If not, it creates a new item and populates it with all relevant information, including:
Ticket subject
Issue description
monday.com item status
Freshservice ticket number
Assigned agent name

During implementation, we encountered a challenge with passing the ticket description to monday.com. The description contained line breaks (\n\n), which caused the API request to fail. To resolve this, we routed the description through a script that extracted only the response from the “Issue Description” field and removed problematic formatting before sending it to monday.com.

The result was a scalable, flexible integration that met SciOps Automations’ needs and can easily be extended to support multiple teams and boards—without being constrained by the limitations of the standard connector.



Once the monday.com item is successfully created, the workflow processes the response returned by the monday.com API. It extracts the newly created item ID and stores it in a custom Freshservice ticket field called “monday.com item id.” This field is then used in future checks to confirm whether a monday.com item already exists for the ticket, preventing duplicate entries.
Finally, the workflow updates the ticket status to a custom state, “Transferred to monday.com,” giving agents clear visibility that the ticket has been successfully handed off to monday.com.

Alerting
This tool has been transformative for our team. Previously, we were receiving around 30 tickets per day related to security alerts that ultimately turned out to be false positives. These tickets consumed valuable engineering time and distorted our operational metrics.
Since implementing the alerting tool, we’ve integrated seven different security platforms (with more planned), enabling us to triage and prioritise alerts far more quickly and efficiently. As a result, we’ve been able to significantly reduce noise without impacting performance—our first-line fix rate has remained stable, while engineers have been freed up to focus on higher-value work.
In addition, we’ve introduced alerting for security events that were not previously tracked effectively. This has improved our overall visibility and, from a cybersecurity perspective, has made our environment measurably more secure. 
We also used to receive emails from our printer service that Ink was running out, however this also generated a lot of other noise as these emails had lots of traffic. This made it very difficult to track printer ink levels. Thanks to workflows and alerts we now receive a ticket once the cartridge is empty & this allows our engineers to respond to these quickly and efficiently. 




Operational Metrics & Performance Improvements
Historically, tracking key metrics such as lost requests and end-to-end SLA performance was challenging. Many requests were submitted via email, limiting visibility within the ITSM platform and resulting in incomplete baseline data for certain measures, particularly around lost or untracked requests.
That said, we do have strong comparative data for SLA performance. Under the previous Cherwell system, SLA attainment averaged around 60%. This was largely driven by low user engagement with the platform, significant back-and-forth to gather missing information or establish ownership, and limited overall ticket visibility.
Since migrating email-based ticket logging into Freshservice, SLA attainment has increased to 94%, representing a 34% improvement. This uplift is primarily due to improved request visibility, more structured intake, clearer routing, and a reduction in rework. While 94% is a strong outcome, we expect further improvements as additional automation is introduced.
We’ve also seen measurable gains in Service Desk First Line Fix (FLF) rates. Previously, FLF averaged around 50%. Through improved workflows, enhanced automation, and greater knowledge availability via the service catalogue, FLF has increased to 65%.
In addition, approximately 15% of tickets are now handled proactively through alerting, rather than being raised by users. When this proactive handling is factored in, the effective improvement in FLF is closer to 30%, representing a significant reduction in manual handling and escalation effort.
The time savings delivered by Fresh have enabled us to significantly upskill our Service Desk staff. As a result, we have been able to transition team members into other areas of the Sanger IT function, while also onboarding new starters at a substantially higher capability level than previously possible. Although this represents a steeper initial learning curve, staff are now reaching a higher level of proficiency in a much shorter timeframe.

By adopting Freshservice, the Wellcome Sanger Institute has:
Eliminated reliance on email-based ticketing
Improved governance through structured approvals and CAB processes
Introduced automation that reduces manual effort
Gained visibility into assets that were never previously tracked
Enabled teams to focus on higher-value work
Started the development of a company wide Service Catalogue
Freshservice now serves as a scalable platform supporting both IT and business services across the Institute.

This does require group allocation and storage allocation to be automated.  To achieve this we have connected FreshService API to rundeck  API which will runs the scripts storage changes.

As our existing change request system is being phased out, we are implementing a Change Advisory Board (CAB) process within Freshservice to support financial system change management. This ensures that all changes related to our current and future ERP platforms are formally reviewed, approved, and governed within a single, auditable system.
Given that our ERP systems are subject to annual financial audits, robust change management is critical to maintaining compliance. By embedding the CAB process in Freshservice, we can demonstrate clear change governance, improve traceability, and support successful audit outcomes across Sanger.
Lustre Quota Requests
To improve disk quota management for our High Performance Computing (HPC) environment, we are developing a dedicated Freshservice request form that integrates directly with automation. Submissions to this form will trigger a workflow that runs a BASH script, which in turn calls a Python script to transfer disk quota between Lustre areas used by different teams.
This process is tightly integrated with Freshservice’s approval workflows, ensuring that quota transfers are reviewed and approved by the appropriate quota owners for each Sanger team or area. The result is a controlled, auditable, and significantly more efficient quota management process for teams that rely heavily on HPC resources.
Access Group Management Automation
To reduce wait times and ensure that requests are processed accurately, we are implementing a fully automated process for Access Group Management. This automation will enable end users to request changes to multiple UNIX groups (adding or removing users) and have Freshservice process those requests instantly.
Workflow Overview:
Retrieve the groups requested for modification.
Cross-reference these with a custom object table that identifies each group’s owner.
Create a child ticket for each unique owner and send an approval request.
Upon approval or rejection, trigger an SSH script on the server to add or remove the user accordingly.
Send an informational email on the parent ticket indicating whether the request was processed or rejected.
Automatically close the parent ticket once all child tickets have been completed.


Currently, the manual process for these requests accounts for approximately 10% of all Service Desk activity. We started using Freshworks because we were facing significant issues with Zendesk’s capabilities, particularly regarding integrations with our project management system. We provide IT support, web development, and digital marketing services primarily in the e-learning space. We handle an extremely high volume of requests for the clients, digital assets, and websites we support. This massive volume of communication, roughly 2,000 to 3,000 emails per month, made our work extremely challenging, especially given the technical nature of the industry where it is critical to get every detail absolutely right.

To address this, we used Freshdesk Omni to provide a diverse support experience for our customers. In our industry, having human support is uncommon, so we wanted to preserve that human touch and make it easy to reach someone exactly when needed. We implemented a multi-channel approach, which included Freshchat via a live widget, SMS, and WhatsApp, alongside standard email support. Later, we added Freshcaller so clients could call us. We even allow customers to meet with our service staff through Zoom meetings, which they can request directly through our live chat methods.

We organized the ticketing space so that the bulk of the work is done inside the Freshdesk ticketing area. We use specific categories tied to "task size" - such as Bug, Small, Medium, or Large - which are equivalent to a certain number of development and support hours from the fulfillment team. We also categorize the type of request (bugs, questions, billing, etc.) to allocate the right resources. We use SLAs to manage response times and service quality, and we utilize various automations to set due dates based on the task size. We also use macros and canned responses to ensure customer service agents include all critical information when responding.

We added additional fields to integrate with our project management system, ClickUp. We use a shared numbering system and task URLs to link the two platforms. We built a custom integration so that when an agent selects a category and sends a message in Freshdesk, it automatically creates a task inside ClickUp where everything is mapped and coordinated. All fulfillment notes are done inside ClickUp, and we use mapped statuses such as "Blocked," "Waiting for Third Party," or "Waiting for Client," to keep both teams in sync. If we are waiting for information, Freshdesk will continue to send automated reminders to the client until we obtain it. Once a status reaches a certain stage in ClickUp, the customer service team knows to communicate the results back to the client. This process has allowed us to maintain human-first customer service in an IT industry where that is becoming increasingly rare.

Since the transition, our customer satisfaction has greatly increased. Clients have praised the different methods available to contact our team and are delighted that they can reach actual humans. This has become a major selling point during discovery calls and helps us win business over competitors. The switch also saved us a lot of money compared to our previous Zendesk installation. The tighter integration with ClickUp and the expanded capabilities within Freshworks are saving a significant amount of time for both the customer service and fulfillment teams. We also have clear notes and history now; if a client discusses an issue from six months ago, we can quickly retrieve that information without wasting time and follow up appropriately.
